text:
emma: FYI eu-west racks 3/4 hit thermal throttle this morning around 03:40UTC. observed degraded GPU clocks and higher latencies for tail tokens.
diego: logs? what triggered it?
emma: stack traces point to a small cohort of tenants spamming long decode streams with batch_size ~256. combined power draw pushed rack temp -> fan ramp -> thermal throttle. logs: https://internal.logs/redwood/eu/4865432100
priya: that lines up with the NVMe write storms too. big streams + large kv regen causing IO bursts.
mikhail: curious if this was admission or scheduling related. were those tenants on preemptible backfill or colocated with reserved slices?
emma: mix. t-900 was on fractional preemptible; t-412 was on shared slice. both had sudden batch size spikes.
diego: immediate mitigation ideas: 1) soft-admit: temporary reduce max_batch for tenants exceeding energy footprint threshold 2) hot-lane reservations for heavy scorers 3) IO pacing on the nodes
priya: +1 soft-admit. we can implement at allocator/proxy level without touching runtime. safer to slow them than preempt.
mikhail: can we compute energy footprint quickly? we have a crude model: footprint = batch_size * sequence_len * qps factor. use that to flag > threshold.
emma: agree. threshold for EU racks set to 1e7 for now (empirical). if footprint>threshold -> apply soft-admit: max_batch=64 and route to preemptible-slices.
priya: config sketch for proxy/allocator rule (canary):
```
# admission rule prototype
- id: soft_admit_eu_v1
  match: region=="eu-west" and footprint > 10000000
  action:
    type: soft_admit
    params: {max_batch: 64, route: preemptible_fractional, hold_ms: 120000}
  canary_pct: 2
```
priya: will PR to staging in 20m.
diego: ops-bot create incident and ticket for postmortem + call tenant owners. tag: eu-thermal-soft-admit
ops-bot: incident INC-486543 created by diego. ticket TKT-486543 added to eng-infra backlog.
finance-bot: alert: preemptible and fractional routing increased dedicated-burst cost estimate by 6% for EU this window.
emma: noted. but cheaper than emergency pool spin-ups and potential customer impact.
mikhail: long term: prefer workload classification and offering a reserved "high-throughput" SKU to tenants doing large batch scoring. that'll be explicit and not surprise infra.
diego: also add node-level IO pacing and a nvme write_coalesce tweak as a follow-up. low-risk kernel knob.
priya: will run canary 2% traffic for t-900 and t-412 immediately. monitor rack temp, gpu clocks, and tok95 latency. alerts: rack_temp>68C for 5m or tok95>400ms.
emma: good. if soft-admit reduces thermal events we can expand to 10% -> 50% next 8h. keep human ack before >50%.
diego: one more ask: add telemetry tag isolation.soft_admit.v1 to billing so we can attribute cost delta.
ops-bot: telemetry tag added to TKT-486543.
finance-bot: FYI please include projected hourly delta in TKT-486543 before large rollouts. small PR will be flagged.
emma: thanks team. keeping thread for concise updates only. post canary numbers in ~30m.
priya: pushed staging rule. beginning test traffic now (trace ids tr-eu-01xxxx).
emma: 16m update: initial 2% canary dropped peak rack_temp from 70C -> 62C and reduced 95th latency from ~520ms -> 190ms for the affected nodes. continuing ramp plan.
diego: nice. prepare rollback steps in case preemptible routing overloads other racks.
mikhail: noted. adding a circuit-breaker: if preemptible_spill_rate>15% abort rollout.
emma: closing loop: if current trend holds, we'll schedule a short postmortem and propose a reserved HT SKU. thanks all.
